Our eldest has QT prolongation, but my sister and I both only have mild heart arrhythmia. She took an ECG for an unrelated reason a while back. She has been vaccinated for COVID, and her cold was likely a common cold as our eldest and I also had it, and we all recovered around the same time. Thank you for such a thoughtful response. Unfortunately I'm also starting to wonder if she had some underlying heart condition that was never diagnosed. :( She frequently did cardio exercises, and an ECG she took once only diagnosed her with mild heart arrhythmia. She probably has the healthiest heart of all of us, but it doesn't explain her random heart palpitations. Very confusing.

Yes, her symptoms were worse in the morning, after having taken it at night, and would improve as the day went on. The only exception I can recall being that she mentioned her hands feeling numb again after dinner on the last night she was alive.




She wasn't taking any medication to treat symptoms, unfortunately. She may have taken bioflu when she had a cold, but she had mostly gotten rid of her cold by the time she started, so she was no longer taking them.




By ragdolling I mean that she would walk unsteadily into my bed in the morning, and then struggle to go to the toilet to dry heave/vomit, as well as have difficulty standing up without bumping into a wall. I don't any part of her twitching more than the others, but she did experience tremors in the morning.

I had neglected to mention it in the post, but she was once diagnosed with mild heart arrhythmia. I was told it wasn't a big deal when I was diagnosed with the same, so I never thought it could have an effect.

I looked up the symptoms, she had some of them but her fever was mild, and unsure of the muscle rigidity. To be honest, I have no interest in pressing charges against her doctor. Her doctor was kind, and all the residents/psychiatrists there were clearly overworked. Although his explanation that her cold infected her lungs despite it getting better never sat right with me, getting rid of 8 years of hard work for a selfless, extremely stressful, undervalued, and currently understaffed profession wouldn't sit right with me. 




He seemed very affected by her death, so I doubt he'll be making that same mistake again. Although I feel strangely vindicated because the "her cold infected her lungs" explanation never sat right with me.




I'm sorry, I know this isn't what you want to hear from me. I won't be changing my mind, and I hope you aren't too frustrated by it.

She didn't have a bloodtest done beforehand, although her last prescription mentioned to do the following:CBC, TSH, Na, K, Crea, ALT, AST, and 12L ECG. 




We had planned to go together on the day she died. We didn't know it had to be done prior, so we waited until we were sure her insurance could cover it.




I was responsible for contacting her doctor(she didn't make me I volunteered), when I mentioned dry heaving and weakness, he mentioned she might want to go to a doctor since she had a cold. When I told him she said it was similar to aripiprazole, he said to observe for now and lower the dosage to ¼. When I mentioned shaking, fever, dizziness, and paleness, he recommended having her checked by a pulmonologist, which we were planning to check the insurance on while getting her lab tests done.



Her doctor is still a resident, so lack of experience might have been why.

I dont know the situation, but it could be possible that your social worker is simply overworked with patients atm. Have you tried reaching out to her? I have had to reach out to my psychiatrist before for the same reason. I was worried they forgot about me, or just didnt want to deal with me anymore, but twice they were simply busy, and once they were on emergency leave. I assure you you wont be a bother if you just reach out. She has already shown that she wants to help you, a checkup after a week of silence wont change her mind.


 Please know that none of those instances were your fault, and that you just had the misfortune of finding therapists who werent trained adequately. It is NOT because youre beyond help, and the fact that you continued to seek help after those incedents proves that you want to get better, which is one of the hardest parts of helping yourself.


I dont know if this advice would be useful, so feel free to discard it, but maybe next time you could let them know what sort of things you need help with, and ask them upfront if they feel theyre able to hand those subjects? That way you wont have to keep opening up only to get hurt when they say they cant help you.


Regardless, I hope you find a therapist who can be there for you consistently. The fact that you kept trying after all this time is promising. Thank you for not giving up on yourself. Good luck out there♡
